message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
It includes both the `gcloud` CLI command (the easiest way) and the equivalent **REST API** payload you could POST to the Compute Engine API if you prefer programmatic control.

> **Prerequisites**  
> * You have a Google Cloud project (`PROJECT_ID`) with billing enabled.  
> * The Compute Engine API is enabled (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).  
> * You have the `gcloud` CLI installed and authenticated (`gcloud auth login`).  
> * You have a service account key if you plan to use the REST API directly.

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Variables – replace with your own values
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports GPUs
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"  # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator=type="$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT" \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

### Optional: Startup Script

Create a `startup.sh` file to install NVIDIA drivers and CUDA (optional but recommended):

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Update package lists
apt-get update

# Install NVIDIA driver (Ubuntu 20.04)
apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470

# Install CUDA Toolkit (if needed)
apt-get install -y cuda-toolkit-11-4

# Reboot to activate drivers (optional)
# reboot
```

Make sure the script is executable:

```bash
chmod +x startup.sh
```

---

## 2. Using the REST API (JSON payload)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine API directly (e.g., from a custom application), you can POST the following JSON to:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
```

Replace `{PROJECT_ID}` and `{ZONE}` with your values.

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "automaticRestart": true
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470\napt-get install -y cuda-toolkit-11-4"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  },
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ]
}
```

### Authentication

When calling the REST API, you’ll need an OAuth 2.0 access token with the scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`.  
You can obtain one via a service account key:

```bash
gcloud auth activate-service-account --key-file=service-account.json
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-access-token)
```

Then include it in the HTTP header:

```
Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN
Content-Type: application/json
```

---

## 3. Verify the Instance

After creation, you can check the instance status:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --project=my-gcp-project \
  --zone=us-central1-a
```

Look for `"status": "RUNNING"` and `"accelerators": [{"acceleratorType":"nvidia-tesla-a6000","acceleratorCount":1}]`.

---

### Quick Checklist

| Step | Command / Action |
|------|------------------|
| Enable Compute Engine API | `gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com` |
| Create instance (CLI) | `gcloud compute instances create ...` |
| Or POST JSON to REST API | `curl -X POST ... -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @payload.json` |
| Verify | `gcloud compute instances describe ...` |

That’s all! You now have a fully functional Compute Engine VM with an RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS. Happy computing!
